rationale: Twenty-fifth pass: repair the eligibility probe and re-execute. The previous run produced thirteen rejections including the first add, which the acceptance predicate explains: with ordered config changes enabled, a change is only up to date when its ConfigChangeId equals the membership's current ConfigChangeId, which starts at zero and becomes the accepted entry index. The first harness supplied 1..13, so every case was rejected as out of order and the matrix is a construction error rather than evidence about eligibility. The successor harness tracks the last accepted index, sets ConfigChangeId from it, and emits the case name, acceptance, supplied ccid and entry index. A fresh execution is requested because the harness changed; the earlier receipt stays in history and is not used as evidence.

experiment.revision_reason: The first harness supplied ConfigChangeId values 1..13 to an ordered membership whose expected id starts at zero, so all cases were rejected as out of order. The successor tracks the last accepted index and supplies it as each change's ConfigChangeId.

scope.description: Apply a fixed sequence of membership changes, supplying the ordered config change id each time, and record acceptance per case.

experiment.prefix: newMembership(1, 1, true) starts with ConfigChangeId zero. The harness increments an entry index per case, sets cc.ConfigChangeId to the last accepted index (starting at zero), applies the change, and advances the tracked id when the change is accepted. Cases: add node 2 at a; add node 2 again; add observer 3 at b; promote observer 3 with the same address; add observer 4 at the duplicate address b; add witness 5 at w; add witness 5 as observer; add witness 5 as node; remove node 2; re-add removed node 2; remove observer 3; remove witness 5; remove node 1 as the only member. Only the membership object is exercised.
